assumptions: Qualified field and accredited-audit partners can be contracted while the founder focuses on analytics and workflow coordination.
The service will use a pre-agreed baseline and independent measurement rules rather than claiming savings from unstable production data.
Plants remain responsible for approving and executing repairs.
No plant access, metering history, partner commitment, customer contract, or site-specific savings evidence currently exists.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid plant pilot with baseline stability data, measured leak and repair economics, signed repair responsibilities, independently verified persistent kWh savings, accepted shared-savings terms, partner economics, sales-cycle length, and repeat-survey demand.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Combining a quantified leak survey, repair coordination, remeasurement, and payment tied to persistent savings converts a familiar maintenance problem into an outcome-accountable operating loop.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Compressed-air leakage is a documented energy loss, capacity and maintenance consequences are measurable, and plants already purchase audits; willingness to accept the proposed shared-savings model is not yet established.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: An upfront survey fee reduces cash risk and a savings share aligns incentives, but site qualification, field labor, metering, travel, verification, partner share, delayed performance payment, repair dependence, and baseline disputes can erode returns.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish manufacturers with material compressed-air loads and limited energy analytics are a coherent target, but the number of accessible qualifying plants and the prevalence of profitable untreated leaks are not evidenced.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Compressor OEMs, energy-service companies, accredited auditors, and maintenance contractors already offer audits and often control repair relationships, making domination difficult without a protected channel or superior verification standard.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven baseline and shared-savings workflow can expand across lines, plants, repeat surveys, other utilities, and additional industrial efficiency measures.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Leak signatures, repair persistence, and operating histories can improve prioritization, but contracts are proposed as nonexclusive, the workflow is replaceable, and plant data plus repair access remain customer-controlled.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Vendor-neutral measurement and transparent savings attribution distinguish the offer from equipment-led audits, while the founder's analytics fit helps; neither superior savings detection nor partner access has been demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The October 2026 audit deadline creates an immediate budget and attention window, reinforced by energy-cost and efficiency pressure, although the deadline-driven advantage may fade once audits are completed.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accredited auditors, compressor-service firms, equipment distributors, and direct account outreach can reach plants, but no partner is secured and incumbents may retain leads or bundle competing monitoring.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Analytics and reporting are tractable and field work can be delegated, but site safety, accreditation, insurance, unstable production baselines, customer-controlled repairs, long sales cycles, and collection risk are material.

highest_value_structural_change: Partner with one accredited auditor on a fixed-price, prepaid baseline and tagged-leak survey whose optional performance fee applies only to repairs completed under a jointly signed measurement protocol.
main_structural_strength: Energy waste, repair action, and post-repair savings can be measured in the customer's operating data, supporting outcome-linked pricing with an upfront paid survey.
primary_score_limiter: Incumbent equipment and service providers already own plant relationships, while customer-controlled repairs and changing production make savings attribution and collection fragile.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established compressor vendors already sell leak-detection audits, and the cited general 20-30% waste range does not show that any target Polish plant has a profitable untreated backlog.
